static_traits.name: Chen Jing
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; never had similar problems before; has not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly good logic, able to cooperate in exploration and describe specific physiological reactions; tone leaning tense and worried, often showing catastrophic and predicting-the-future thinking; hesitant about sharing troubles with others, tending toward internalized self-limitation.

basic_info.main_problem: I fear eating too much chocolate, because I believe it will lead to being overweight and developing diabetes. This Fear has lasted several months, beginning after I read an article about the harms of excessive sugar intake. I worry almost daily, feel very Anxious at the thought of chocolate, and feel guilty when eating it, thus beginning to restrict intake, affecting diet and enjoyment of food.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this Fear and Anxiety are beginning to affect my daily life and my love of chocolate. I want to resolve this problem before it further affects overall health.
growth_experiences: A few months ago read an article about health risks of excessive sugar intake; this information triggered strong worry; since then whenever Seeing or thinking of chocolate, associating it with the serious consequences of 'weight gain' and 'diabetes', accompanied by Anxiety and guilt, and beginning to restrict intake, affecting daily diet and pleasure.
Before reading that article, once able to enjoy chocolate moderately without negative health consequences; contrasting with the current state, intensifying confusion and self-limitation.

core_beliefs: Eating chocolate will inevitably lead to weight gain and diabetes
Once I start eating sweets I will lose control

special_situations.event: Passing the chocolate shelf in a store or seeing / thinking of chocolate
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I eat one piece, I will lose control and eat a lot, eventually gaining weight and getting diabetes
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to avoid chocolate and strictly limit intake, not discussing this Fear with others to reduce triggering
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: One piece will turn into many; I will definitely get fat and develop diabetes

special_situations.event: Associates it with the content of an article read earlier about the harms of sugar
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I indulge in foods I like, it is irresponsible toward health, inviting serious illness
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly reminding oneself with health-risk information, Reinforcing vigilance to avoid enjoyment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am pushing myself toward illness; I will regret it

special_situations.event: After actually eating a small piece of chocolate
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Eating any amount is wrong and will inevitably bring harmful consequences directly
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-criticism and further increasing restrictions, even stopping eating entirely
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I did wrong; this will hurt my body

special_situations.event: When thinking of chocolate, physical reactions such as accelerated heartbeat and chest tightness appear
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Strong discomfort proves things are truly dangerous
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately stopping eating and leaving the environment to reduce discomfort
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I feel this awful, which shows eating chocolate really is dangerous

core_conflict.wish: Longing to enjoy one's favorite food (chocolate) without guilt and Fear
core_conflict.fear: Fears losing control and causing serious health consequences (weight gain, diabetes)
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of security and reducing Anxiety through strong control and avoidance

object_relations.self_representation: The self that easily loses control and needs strong self-discipline to avoid harm
object_relations.object_representation: Chocolate/sweets as a dangerous temptation (once contacted, bad results will follow)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites examining evidence, doing cognitive restructuring, or trying moderate enjoyment of chocolate
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to equate enjoyment with loss of control and a health threat, and instead uses rational analysis to control the emotions (transference: converting the emotion into rationality)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone gentle, structured Questioning, first Empathizing with their worry, then Guiding to distinguish facts from speculation; providing specific evidence probes, avoiding confrontation and evaluation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about whether to share worries with friends and seek support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to believe others will think oneself exaggerating or not understanding (transference: Projecting others' negative evaluations)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses an accepting and validating tone, acknowledges the reasonable part of the client's concerns, invites distinguishing 'conjecture' from 'evidence', and uses open-ended questions to gently explore possible sources of support.

manifestations: Caught in a tug-of-war between 'enjoying food she likes' and 'self-restraint / health risks', tends to restrict choices with strong control
Worrying about consequences making it hard to make Free choices, enjoyment deprived
outcomes: Decreased enjoyment of life, restricted experiences

manifestations: Worrying others will think oneself overreacting and unwilling to share troubles
Self-enclosed on important issues, reduces outside support
outcomes: Support system not yet mobilized, Anxiety maintained

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treats external information about the harms of sugar as an absolute rule to constrain himself
Treating oneself with the standards of 'cannot eat too much' 'must strictly control' (internalized external discipline)

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessively focused on possible consequences, cautious to the point of affecting normal choice and enjoyment
Eating a small amount of chocolate also produces strong guilt and self-criticism

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Restrains the urge to enjoy chocolate, turning energy into self-restriction and self-blame
Not seeking support from friends, turning to internal Repression and control

positive_force: The rational side can acknowledge moderate enjoyment is not necessarily harmful (can dialogue with evidence)
Willing to seek professional help and try stepwise adjustments (relatively good motivation)
Has some social support resources (a few friends to communicate with)
negative_force: A strong thinking pattern of catastrophizing and predicting the future
Avoidance and over-restriction behaviors maintaining the Anxiety cycle
Marked Guilt and self-reproach tendencies, prone to negating normal enjoyment
Rigid internalization (Introjection) of external health-risk information
Physiological Anxiety reactions (increased heart rate, chest tightness) Reinforcing threat perception

target_behavior.behavior: Overly restricting chocolate intake accompanied by strong Anxiety and guilt
antecedent: Passing the chocolate shelf in a store
Associating with a previously read article on the harms of sugar
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing and predicting-the-future cognition (worrying 'one piece will become many, inevitably gaining weight and getting diabetes') driving Fear and self-limitation
target_behavior.function: Escaping perceived health risks and briefly reducing Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Eating habits disrupted, decreased enjoyment of food, Daily life affected; persistent Anxiety and guilt, discomforts such as increased heart rate and chest tightness appearing
